Expected outcomes include better feature discriminability, improved boundary localization, and stronger geometric consistency across panoramic views, validated via ablations and comparisons to ERP/CMP baselines.
AI.conclusion: TDFNet demonstrates the value of integrating multiple projection representations with geometry-aware fusion for panoramic salient object detection, achieving improved robustness to projection distortions and offering a strong baseline for multi-projection fusion approaches.

title: Frequency-aware forecasting for short-term typhoon gust prediction
summary: Accurate gust forecasting under typhoon conditions remains challenging due to the highly non-stationary and multi-scale characteristics of extreme wind fluctuations. Existing deep learning models often struggle to simultaneously capture long-term trends and rapid local variations, resulting in degraded performance during extreme events. We propose WDANet, a frequency-aware forecasting framework that integrates stationary wavelet decomposition, a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) strategy, and a dual-branch encoder-decoder architecture, enabling separate modeling of trend and fluctuation components. Taking the offshore regions of the Western Pacific in China as an example, we conduct fine-grid wind gust prediction research. The results demonstrate that WDANet shows advantages for short lead times under the experimental setting across a 24-h forecasting horizon and achieves higher prediction accuracy than ECMWF-HRES within the first 6 h. During extreme wind events, WDANet more accurately captures gust peaks and attains the best RMSE and MAE performance. These results highlight its potential for offshore wind power operation, disaster warning, and risk mitigation.

AI.tldr: WDANet proposes a frequency-aware wind gust forecasting model that decomposes signals into trend and fluctuation using stationary wavelet decomposition, with FiLM-based feature modulation and a dual-branch encoder–decoder to improve short-term and extreme-event predictions, outperforming ECMWF-HRES within 6 hours on offshore Western Pacific gust data.
AI.motivation: Forecasting wind gusts under typhoon-like, non-stationary, multi-scale conditions is challenging due to rapid local fluctuations and evolving trends. Accurate short-horizon predictions are crucial for offshore wind operation, disaster warning, and risk mitigation.
AI.method: WDANet integrates stationary wavelet decomposition to separate frequency components, applies a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) for adaptive feature conditioning, and employs a dual-branch encoder–decoder architecture to separately model trend and fluctuation components, enabling frequency-aware forecasting for 24-h wind gust prediction.
AI.result: WDANet achieves higher accuracy than ECMWF-HRES within the first 6 hours and provides better RMSE and MAE, particularly capturing gust peaks during extreme wind events, across a 24-h forecasting horizon for offshore Western Pacific gust data.
AI.conclusion: WDANet demonstrates superior short-horizon gust forecasting under typhoon conditions and shows potential for enhancing offshore wind power operation, disaster warning, and risk mitigation, by effectively modeling both trend and fluctuation components.

title: Label-Free Foundational Model Selection for Medical Image Classification under Distribution Shift via Pseudo Label Discrepancy
comment: Accepted at MIRASOL Workshop, MICCAI 2026. 10 pages, 3 figures
summary: Foundation models are increasingly deployed for medical image analysis. However, under the inter-institutional distribution shift typical of deployment, their performance varies widely and cannot be known without target-domain labels, which are rarely available. This leaves a practical question unresolved: given several candidate foundational models and labeled-data from a source domain, which one to deploy in an unlabeled target domain? We propose a label-free selection criterion built on SUDO, a framework for evaluating clinical AI systems without ground-truth annotations. SUDO partitions the unlabeled target data by predicted probability and, for each region, measures a pseudo-label discrepancy reflecting class contamination; aggregated across regions, this yields a score (AURCC) requiring neither target annotation nor fine-tuning. We show that AURCC can be used to rank a variety of vision-language models (BioMedCLIP, CXR-CLIP, CheXzero, MedCLIP, MedImageInsight, CLIP) on chest X-ray classification across three inter-hospital shift scenarios, under zero-shot and MLP-probe regimes. The AURCC ranking recovers the ground-truth ranking with Spearman rho up to 0.943 (p<0.05). Against the natural baseline of ranking by held-out source accuracy, AURCC is competitive when the labeled source is large and yields a more accurate ranking once it is small; the regime of interest in resource-constrained settings.

AI.tldr: A label-free model-selection criterion (AURCC) based on SUDO ranks vision-language medical models for unlabeled target domains under distribution shift; achieves high correlation with ground-truth ranking (Spearman up to 0.943) and outperforms source-accuracy ranking when target labels are scarce, enabling robust model deployment without target annotations.
AI.motivation: Address deployment under inter-institutional distribution shift in medical image analysis and the practical need to select among multiple foundation models without access to target-domain labels or fine-tuning.
AI.method: Leverage SUDO, partition unlabeled target data by predicted probability, compute pseudo-label discrepancy reflecting class contamination in each region, aggregate into AURCC score; evaluate across chest X-ray classification using multiple models (BioMedCLIP, CXR-CLIP, CheXzero, MedCLIP, MedImageInsight, CLIP) under three inter-hospital shift scenarios, in zero-shot and MLP-probe regimes.
AI.result: AURCC ranking recovers the ground-truth ranking with Spearman rho up to 0.943 (p<0.05). In comparison with ranking by held-out source accuracy, AURCC is competitive when the source-labeled data is large and becomes more accurate as the source data shrinks, appealing in resource-constrained settings.
AI.conclusion: AURCC provides a practical, label-free criterion for selecting among foundation models under distribution shift, enabling reliable deployment decisions in unlabeled target domains without target annotations or model finetuning.

title: DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search
summary: Industrial e-commerce search systems ultimately aim to optimize the user-level long-term objective, such as n-day cumulative purchases or gross merchandise value (GMV) per user. However, such objectives are defined at the user level, whereas search ranking is based on item-level scores within each request. Existing methods typically bridge this granularity gap through manually designed multi-objective fusion, where predictions of multiple item-level objectives, such as clicks, carts, purchases, and transaction value, are combined into a ranking score that serves as a proxy for the ultimate objective. Such hand-crafted fusion schemes rely on a small set of manually tuned weights, limiting fine-grained personalization and leading to suboptimal alignment with the ultimate objective. In this paper, we propose DCEO (Direct Causal Effect Optimization), a data-driven framework for learning item-level proxy scores that are better aligned with the ultimate objective. We first aggregate the item-level proxy scores into a user-level proxy metric and quantify its alignment with the ultimate objective using a relative causal effect. We then develop an actor-critic framework, where the critic estimates the ultimate objective for a given user-level proxy metric, and the actor dynamically generates context-dependent fusion weights over multiple objectives to construct the item-level proxy scores and is trained to directly optimize the relative causal effect. Extensive offline experiments and analyses demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of DCEO. In addition, DCEO has been deployed in a large-scale industrial e-commerce search system, outperforming the conventional GMV proxy by 0.36% in GMV in a 41-day online A/B test.

AI.tldr: DCEO directly optimizes the alignment between item-level proxy scores and the user-level ultimate objective in industrial e-commerce search via an actor-critic framework that learns context-dependent fusion weights across multiple objectives.
AI.motivation: Bridge the granularity gap between item-level ranking and user-level long-term goals (e.g., GMV per user) and overcome limitations of hand-crafted multi-objective fusion with fixed weights.
AI.method: Aggregate item-level proxies into a user-level proxy; quantify alignment with the ultimate objective via relative causal effect; use an actor-critic setup where the critic predicts the ultimate objective from the user-level proxy and the actor learns context-dependent fusion weights to generate item-level proxies, optimizing the relative causal effect.
AI.result: Offline experiments show effectiveness and interpretability; deployed in a large-scale industrial system; achieved a 0.36% GMV improvement in a 41-day online A/B test compared to the conventional GMV proxy.
AI.conclusion: DCEO provides a data-driven, interpretable framework that improves alignment with the ultimate objective over hand-crafted fusion, with proven online gains in industry deployment.

title: Steer the Sampling, Not the Kernel Grid: Geometry-Guided Sampling Operator for Volumetric Segmentation
summary: Accurate 3D segmentation is central to quantitative lesion assessment and anatomy mapping for clinical planning and follow-up. Thin, elongated, and fine anatomical/pathological structures (e.g., vessels) are a particularly challenging case: a one-voxel boundary error can disconnect a branch and change clinically relevant topology. In encoder-decoder networks (e.g., U-Net), repeated downsampling and fixed-grid convolution blur or alias fine structures and weaken orientation cues, so early mistakes propagate across scales. We propose a geometry-guided local operator that steers where features are sampled, rather than deforming convolutional kernels, under a single formulation for both feature refinement (stride 1) and resolution reduction (stride > 1). At each voxel, it predicts a local orientation and bounded step sizes, samples symmetrically along these directions, and transforms paired samples into compact geometric and boundary cues with lightweight mixing; a cross-scale consensus aligns encoder and decoder features at skip connections to reduce geometric mismatch. Replacing all stride 1 and stride 2 operators in a 3D U-Net yields consistent improvements on BraTS, MSD Hepatic Vessel, and TDSC-ABUS, with notably better boundary metrics (e.g., BraTS Dice 86.1 to 88.9, HD95 7.1 to 6.2; TDSC-ABUS HD95 39.1 to 27.8) while reducing parameters from 2.3M to 0.8M. We further demonstrate that the operator can be integrated into other backbones (e.g., nnU-Net, Swin-UNETR, and MedNeXt) without changing their macro-architectures while providing consistent performance gains.

AI.tldr: A geometry-guided local operator replaces standard stride-based sampling in 3D U-Nets to preserve thin structures and topology in segmentation, achieving boundary improvements with fewer parameters and broad compatibility across backbones.
AI.motivation: Thin, elongated structures such as vessels are highly sensitive to downsampling blur and shortcut topology errors in encoder-decoder nets. A per-voxel orientation-guided sampling strategy aims to maintain geometry and boundary cues across scales.
AI.method: Introduce a per-voxel local orientation predictor with bounded step sizes. Sample symmetrically along predicted directions and fuse samples into geometric/boundary cues with lightweight mixing. Apply a cross-scale consensus at skip connections to align encoder/decoder features. Replace all stride-1 and stride-2 operators in a 3D U-Net; demonstrate integration into backbones like nnU-Net, Swin-UNETR, and MedNeXt, without changing macro-architectures.
AI.result: Consistent improvements on BraTS, MSD Hepatic Vessel, and TDSC-ABUS. Notable boundary metric gains (BraTS Dice 86.1→88.9; HD95 7.1→6.2; TDSC-ABUS HD95 39.1→27.8) with parameter reduction from 2.3M to 0.8M. The operator also integrates into other backbones, maintaining macro-architectures and delivering gains.
AI.conclusion: The geometry-guided local operator yields robust performance gains and model-size reduction, is portable across common 3D segmentation backbones, and addresses boundary/topology preservation for thin structures.

title: A Token-Level Analysis of Sampled-Token Reverse-KL On-Policy Distillation
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures; v2 adds Boyang Liu and Junlin Shang to the author list; scientific content unchanged
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) supervises a student on its own trajectories with token-level signals from a frozen teacher, yet how a sampled loss allocates updates across tokens remains poorly understood. We analyze the gradient of the per-token K2 estimator of reverse KL with respect to the student logits. The $\ell_1$ norm of this gradient factorizes into the absolute teacher--student log-probability gap and a student-side softmax factor that grows as the sampled token becomes less likely under the student. In our math-distillation runs, these per-token norms are highly non-uniform: low-student-probability tokens account for a disproportionate share of their sum and are also enriched in large teacher--student gaps. As a lightweight intervention suggested by this analysis, we study Surprise-aware Reweighting (SuRe), a detached, bounded weighting rule that further amplifies this existing allocation. Across two Qwen3 student scales, SuRe improves several math metrics over vanilla OPD and shows no clear degradation on the selected out-of-domain benchmarks. Our primary contribution is therefore a gradient-level characterization of reverse-KL OPD trained with the K2 estimator, with SuRe as one empirical instantiation.

AI.tldr: A gradient-level analysis of on-policy distillation (OPD) with the per-token K2 estimator of reverse KL reveals highly non-uniform token updates, driven by hard tokens with large teacher–student gaps. The authors propose Surprise-aware Reweighting (SuRe), a detached, bounded reweighting rule, which amplifies these allocations. Empirically, SuRe improves math-related metrics on two Qwen3 student scales compared to vanilla OPD and does not show clear degradation on selected out-of-domain benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To understand how the sampled per-token loss in OPD allocates updates across tokens, and whether a gradient-aware reweighting can improve efficiency and performance.
AI.method: Derive and analyze the gradient of the per-token K2 estimator of reverse KL with respect to student logits. Show that the L1 norm factorizes into a product of (i) the teacher–student log-probability gap and (ii) a student-softmax factor that increases for low-probability tokens. Conduct math-distillation experiments, and introduce Surprise-aware Reweighting (SuRe) as a detached, bounded weighting rule. Evaluate on two Qwen3 student scales, comparing against vanilla OPD, focusing on math-related metrics and out-of-domain robustness.
AI.result: The per-token gradient norms are highly non-uniform; low-probability tokens contribute disproportionately and exhibit large teacher–student gaps. SuRe amplifies this allocation. Across two Qwen3 scales, SuRe improves multiple math metrics over vanilla OPD and shows no clear degradation on selected out-of-domain benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Provides a gradient-level characterization of reverse-KL OPD trained with the K2 estimator, and demonstrates SuRe as a practical augmentation to bias updates toward tokens with larger informative gaps.

title: FlowMoDL: Model-Based Deep Learning with Conjugate-Gradient Data Consistency for Highly Accelerated 4D Flow MRI Reconstruction
summary: We present FlowMoDL, an unrolled neural network for highly accelerated 4D flow MRI reconstruction that directly optimizes for both anatomical magnitude and phase-derived velocity accuracy. Building on the MoDL framework, FlowMoDL alternates a learned (3+1)D spatiotemporal denoiser with conjugate-gradient data-consistency updates based on the SENSE forward model. A novel dual-pathway conditioning scheme adapts the denoiser features and data-consistency weighting, enabling a single model to handle varying acceleration factors ($10\times$ to $50\times$). To ensure physiological accuracy, the network is trained using a deep-supervision composite loss that explicitly penalizes velocity magnitude and angular errors, stabilized by a curriculum schedule. We evaluate FlowMoDL on the multi-center CMRx4DFlow dataset against classical and deep-learning baselines (CG-SENSE, MoDL, FlowVN, and FlowMRI-Net). A key advantage of FlowMoDL is its superior gradient step efficiency. When evaluated under an equivalent, limited budget of gradient steps, competing flow-specific networks degrade significantly. In contrast, FlowMoDL robustly converges and strictly outperforms all competitors across all acceleration factors in magnitude SSIM, nRMSE, relative velocity error, and angular error, successfully recovering sharp structural details and temporally coherent velocity fields.

AI.tldr: FlowMoDL is an unrolled network for accelerated 4D flow MRI that jointly optimizes magnitude and velocity accuracy via a (3+1)D denoiser with CG data-consistency, featuring dual-pathway conditioning to handle 10–50x acceleration and deep-supervision losses for velocity metrics; it achieves state-of-the-art results and superior gradient-step efficiency across accelerations.
AI.motivation: The need to reconstruct accurate 4D flow MRI under very high acceleration while preserving velocity-derived metrics and anatomical detail. Existing methods struggle with speed, accuracy, and generalization across centers and high acceleration factors.
AI.method: An unrolled architecture extending MoDL (FlowMoDL) that alternates a learned (3+1)D spatiotemporal denoiser with conjugate-gradient data-consistency updates based on a SENSE forward model. A dual-pathway conditioning scheme adapts denoiser features and data-consistency weighting to handle 10×–50× acceleration. Training uses a deep-supervision composite loss that explicitly penalizes velocity magnitude and angular errors, stabilized by a curriculum schedule. Evaluation on the multi-center CMRx4DFlow dataset versus CG-SENSE, MoDL, FlowVN, and FlowMRI-Net.
AI.result: FlowMoDL exhibits superior gradient-step efficiency; with an equal gradient-step budget, competing flow-specific networks degrade, while FlowMoDL converges robustly and outperforms all baselines across all accelerations on magnitude SSIM, nRMSE, relative velocity error, and angular error, preserving sharp anatomy and temporally coherent velocity fields.
AI.conclusion: FlowMoDL delivers state-of-the-art, efficient reconstruction for accelerated 4D flow MRI, driven by dual-pathway conditioning and deep supervision that enhance magnitude and velocity accuracy and generalize across acceleration factors and centers.

title: LDAC-Net: A Learnable Multi-Lag Differencing Attention-Convolution Network for Drift-Robust Recognition with Low-Cost MOX Gas Sensors
summary: Portable electronic-nose systems based on low-cost metal-oxide (MOX) gas sensors offer a practical solution for gas and odour recognition, but their signals are affected by slow chemical transients, drifting sensor offsets, scale variation, and cross-channel correlations. Existing pipelines commonly use fixed first-order temporal differencing (FOTD), which requires a manually selected lag and may discard useful response information. We propose LDAC-Net, an end-to-end learnable multi-lag differencing attention-convolution network that operates directly on multi-channel MOX signals. Its learnable differential feature enhancement front-end combines window-conditioned statistical affine normalisation, which compensates for window-specific offset and scale variation, with learnable multi-lag differencing, which weights and combines temporal differences across multiple lags. A compact attention-convolution backbone subsequently models local transients and longer-range temporal dependencies. On the 50-class SmellNet-Base task, LDAC-Net achieves 68.2% top-1 accuracy, exceeding the best FOTD-preprocessed comparison model by approximately 14 percentage points and the raw-input Transformer by more than 30 points. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of both proposed components. The representation also transfers to SmellNet-Mixtures, improving accuracy from 45.4% to 50.5%, and generalises to the 62-channel eNose-Drift benchmark under strong long-term drift, achieving 70.6% top-1 accuracy and 69.6% macro-F1. These results outperform the best comparison model with dataset-retuned FOTD preprocessing by 8.0 and 3.0 points, respectively, demonstrating that learnable, sensor-aware preprocessing is more effective than fixed handcrafted differencing for low-cost MOX gas-sensor recognition.

AI.tldr: LDAC-Net is an end-to-end learnable multi-lag differencing attention-convolution network for portable MOX gas sensors, outperforming fixed first-order differencing and raw-input transformers across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: MOX-based portable e-noses suffer from slow chemical transients, drift, scale variation, and cross-channel correlations. Fixed first-order temporal differencing (FOTD) requires manual lag choice and can discard useful information; there is a need for sensor-aware, learnable preprocessing to improve recognition.
AI.method: Propose LDAC-Net with a learnable differential feature enhancement front-end that uses window-conditioned statistical affine normalisation to compensate for offset/scale variation and learnable multi-lag differencing to weight and combine temporal differences across multiple lags, followed by a compact attention-convolution backbone to model local transients and longer-range dependencies.
AI.result: On 50-class SmellNet-Base: 68.2% top-1, ~14 pp above best FOTD-preprocessed model and >30 pp above raw-input Transformer. Ablations confirm contributions of both components. Transfer to SmellNet-Mixtures: accuracy 45.4%→50.5%. Generalises to 62-channel eNose-Drift: 70.6% top-1, 69.6% macro-F1, outperforming dataset-retuned FOTD-based models by 8.0 and 3.0 pp respectively.
AI.conclusion: Learnable, sensor-aware preprocessing with multi-lag differencing and attention-convolution yields superior performance and drift robustness compared with fixed handcrafted differencing for low-cost MOX gas-sensor recognition, with good transferability across datasets.

title: Socialized Detector Learning: Trajectory-Guided and Reciprocal Distillation for Heterogeneous Object Detectors
summary: Object detection knowledge is fragmented across independently trained, heterogeneous detectors with complementary category supports. In socialized learning, this knowledge resides in a society, and learning aims to evolve the society collectively through exchange. However, aggregation-based socialization does not explicitly plan transfer order, whereas progressive multi-teacher distillation considers order but remains a one-way student enhancement in a shared category space. Building on Socialized Learning, we formulate Socialized Detector Learning (SDL) for heterogeneous, category-specialized object detectors and propose Trajectory-Guided and Reciprocal Distillation (TGRD).TGRD estimates directed operational Inter-Detector Transfer Difficulty (IDTD) from held-out feature-alignment residuals, precomputes a fixed score table, and greedily constructs a carrier trajectory. Along the trajectory, knowledge is progressively consolidated into a union-category carrier and then returned to experts through reciprocal transfer. A conditional proxy-certificate analysis shows that, under stated assumptions, the progressive certificate is no larger than an aggregated-target counterpart. On MS COCO with four heterogeneous experts and two carrier initializations, final carriers outperform epoch-matched simultaneous aggregation controls by 2.6 AP in both settings. Reciprocal detectors attain 20.8--28.4 AP on previously unsupported categories while remaining within 1.3 AP of original expert-specific performance. These results support order-aware progressive consolidation followed by reciprocal transfer as a viable mechanism for detector-society evolution.

AI.tldr: Proposes Socialized Detector Learning (SDL) with Trajectory-Guided and Reciprocal Distillation (TGRD) to enable order-aware, progressive consolidation of heterogeneous, category-specialized detectors, followed by reciprocal transfer. Demonstrates improved detection performance and coverage on MS COCO over aggregation-based baselines.
AI.motivation: Knowledge in object-detection detectors is fragmented across heterogeneous models with complementary category supports. Existing aggregation lacks transfer-order planning and one-way distillation limits knowledge sharing. SDL with TGRD aims to orchestrate directed, progressive knowledge transfer to and from a shared carrier.
AI.method: Introduce SDL framework and TGRD. Estimate directed Inter-Detector Transfer Difficulty (IDTD) from held-out feature-alignment residuals, precompute a fixed score table, and greedily construct a carrier trajectory that progressively consolidates knowledge into a union-category carrier, then performs reciprocal transfer back to experts. Provide a conditional proxy-certificate analysis showing progress certificate size is bounded relative to aggregated targets.
AI.result: On MS COCO with four heterogeneous experts and two carrier initializations, final carriers outperform epoch-matched simultaneous aggregation controls by 2.6 AP in both setups. Reciprocal detectors achieve 20.8–28.4 AP on previously unsupported categories while staying within 1.3 AP of the original expert performances.
AI.conclusion: Order-aware progressive consolidation followed by reciprocal transfer is a viable mechanism for detector-society evolution, enabling improved overall performance and expanded category coverage without substantial loss to individual expert accuracy.

title: Adversarial Training of Linear Models under Stealthy Attacks
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: Predictive models are widely used in many fields, but are vulnerable to false data injection attacks. To address this, detection schemes and adversarial training have been proposed, but such approaches lack guarantees against stealthy attacks. We therefore propose a detector-based switched model, in which optimal attack strategies are stealthy. For linear prediction models, we derive a convex formulation of the resulting adversarial risk. The model incorporates protected features and introduces a hyperparameter modelling attack probability, enabling an explicit performance trade-off between clean and attacked data regimes. Numerical simulations on real and synthetic data show improved performance on partially attacked data, even for misspecified attack probabilities.

AI.tldr: Proposes a detector-based switched model to defend against false data injection attacks. Derives a convex adversarial-risk formulation for linear predictors, incorporating protected features and an attack-probability hyperparameter to trade off clean vs attacked data. Demonstrates improvements on partially attacked data via simulations, even when attack probability is misspecified.
AI.motivation: Predictive models are vulnerable to false data injection; existing detectors and adversarial training lack guarantees against stealthy attacks; aim to provide provable performance guarantees under stealthy attack strategies.
AI.method: Detector-based switched model; convex formulation of adversarial risk for linear models; includes protected features; hyperparameter for attack probability; evaluation on real and synthetic data.
AI.result: Convex adversarial-risk formulation; improved performance on data partially attacked; robustness holds under misspecified attack probabilities.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers explicit trade-offs and finite-sample protections against stealthy data attacks for linear predictors, leveraging a detector-based switching mechanism.

title: THA-Flow Generative Model: Prosthesis Geometry Prediction from Preoperative CT
summary: Preoperative planning for total hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly framed as selecting a single prosthesis configuration and placement for a patient's osseous anatomy. In practice, however, the same anatomy may admit several clinically reasonable solutions, making planning inherently a one-to-many problem that is better represented by a conditional probability distribution. We present THA-Flow, a conditional flow-matching model that generates three-dimensional prosthesis geometry directly from preoperative CT. Separate AutoencoderKL models compress preoperative bone anatomy and prosthesis geometry, while a three-dimensional UNet learns a rectified flow from Gaussian noise to the prosthesis latent space under spatial bone conditioning and optional structured prosthesis parameters. The retrospective cohort comprised 1,355 hips from 1,149 patients undergoing primary THA. Following rigid registration of postoperative CT to preoperative CT, the actual postoperative prostheses were transformed independently according to the pelvic and femoral registrations and represented as a dual-channel truncated signed distance field. The prosthesis autoencoder achieved a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 47.11 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.9964 on the validation set. Complete acetabular and femoral geometries were generated across seven major stem models representing 93.4% of the cohort. Repeated bone-conditioned sampling preserved component position, alignment, and the principal bone-prosthesis interfaces while allowing limited local geometric variation. To our knowledge, THA-Flow represents the first application of generative AI to three-dimensional surgical planning for THA.

AI.tldr: THA-Flow is a conditional flow-matching model that generates 3D prosthesis geometries for total hip arthroplasty directly from preoperative CT, framing planning as a conditional one-to-many distribution.
AI.motivation: Preoperative THA planning is inherently one-to-many: a patient anatomy may admit multiple clinically acceptable prosthesis configurations. A generative, probabilistic approach can enumerate viable options and preserve bone-prosthesis relationships.
AI.method: Two AutoencoderKL networks compress preoperative bone anatomy and prosthesis geometry; a 3D UNet learns a rectified flow from Gaussian noise to the prosthesis latent space under bone conditioning and optional structured prosthesis parameters; postoperative CTs are registered to preop CT and converted to dual-channel truncated signed distance fields; training on 1,355 hips from 1,149 patients; seven stem models cover 93.4% of cohort.
AI.result: The prosthesis autoencoder achieved PSNR 47.11 dB and SSIM 0.9964 on validation; complete acetabular/femoral geometries generated for seven stem models; repeated bone-conditioned sampling preserved component position/alignment and bone-prosthesis interfaces with local geometric variation; THA-Flow is the first application of generative AI to 3D THA planning.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates feasibility of a generative, bone-conditioned 3D planning tool for THA that can produce multiple viable prosthesis configurations while maintaining critical anatomical interfaces.

title: Modeling spatio-temporal locality in multi-step forecasting of geo-referenced time series
summary: Forecasting future measurements from geographically distributed sensors is essential across many domains. However, the spatial distribution of these sensors raises multiple challenges, primarily due to spatial autocorrelation phenomena, that introduce inter-dependencies among nearby locations, that cannot therefore be treated independently. While some existing approaches can capture such phenomena, they generally model the spatial dimension globally across all locations. On the other hand, the method we propose in this paper, called SPALT, focuses on capturing spatial relationships among time series with similar trends, even if they occur at different times, thus modeling the spatio-temporal locality. SPALT leverages linear model trees, which allow us to consider the spatial autocorrelation locally: during the tree-building process, the adopted heuristics group time series exhibiting similar trends into the same node, on which additional features considering the spatial dimension are selectively injected. Additionally, we propose a new pruning strategy, based on Reduced Error Pruning, that also considers the spatio-temporal locality during the tree simplification. Designed for a multi-step setting, SPALT provides forecasts for multiple future time steps across multiple sensors simultaneously. The characteristics exhibited by SPALT can provide significant benefits in different domains, where measurements come from distributed sensors. In this paper, we focus on data produced by sensors located in multiple renewable power plants measuring their energy production at regular, short intervals. Experiments on 3 real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SPALT in forecasting the production of energy at different time horizons, and its superior performance in comparison with tree-based models and state-of-the-art neural networks that incorporate both temporal and spatial dimensions.

AI.tldr: SPALT is a locality-aware spatio-temporal forecasting method using linear model trees to group time series by similar trends and selectively inject spatial features; it includes a new Reduced Error Pruning strategy and supports multi-step, multi-sensor forecasts, showing superior accuracy on renewable-energy datasets.
AI.motivation: To address spatial autocorrelation and limitations of global spatial models by capturing locally similar-trend time series and their spatial dependencies for accurate multi-step forecasts across distributed sensors.
AI.method: Builds a linear model tree; during split decisions, groups time series with similar trends into the same node; injects spatial features selectively at nodes; uses Reduced Error Pruning that accounts for spatio-temporal locality; supports multi-step forecasts across sensors.
AI.result: Empirical results on three real-world renewable-energy datasets show SPALT outperforms traditional tree-based models and state-of-the-art neural networks that jointly model space and time.
AI.conclusion: Local, trend-homogeneous regional modeling via SPALT improves forecast accuracy for distributed sensor networks and is applicable across domains with spatio-temporal data.

title: DEFUSE: Generalizable Backdoor Defense for Self-Supervised Encoders with Generative Priors
summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing threats to both visual SSL encoders and vision-language encoders. Existing defenses are typically designed for only one of these paradigms and rely on restrictive assumptions such as access to uninfected in-distribution data or precomputed pseudo-labels, which are difficult to satisfy in practice. To address these limitations, we propose DEFUSE, a generalizable backdoor detection framework for SSL encoders. Inspired by Bayesian posterior inference, we reformulate backdoor detection as a representation-conditioned image likelihood estimation problem parameterized by a conditional diffusion generative model. Uninfected representations tend to yield semantically consistent reconstructions, whereas backdoored ones are more likely to be mapped to the attacker's target class or semantically meaningless images, deviating from the original semantics and thereby exposing the backdoor. However, we find that the exact likelihood is intractable, because highly abstracted representations discard the low-level information necessary for pixel-faithful reconstruction. We therefore relax the objective to semantic reconstruction and evaluate it in a well-separated representation space provided by a reference encoder. Rather than training from scratch, we fine-tune a pretrained diffusion model, leveraging its generative prior to map data onto the natural image manifold while preserving semantic content. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DEFUSE substantially outperforms existing detectors across diverse attack settings, generalizing to both visual SSL and vision-language encoders. Notably, our method greatly reduces the reliance on prior knowledge about the victim encoder or the attack strategy. The source code is available at https://github.com/jsrdcht/DEFUSE .

AI.tldr: DEFUSE is a generalizable backdoor detector for SSL and vision-language encoders that uses a diffusion-based semantic reconstruction approach conditioned on representations, avoiding strong data/label assumptions and outperforming prior detectors.
AI.motivation: Backdoor attacks threaten SSL and vision-language encoders. Existing defenses are siloed (one paradigm) and rely on uninfected data or pseudo-labels, which are impractical. A generalizable, assumption-light detector is needed.
AI.method: Recast backdoor detection as a representation-conditioned image likelihood estimation via a conditional diffusion model. Since exact likelihood is intractable, adopt semantic reconstruction in a representation space provided by a reference encoder. Fine-tune a pretrained diffusion model rather than training from scratch to map inputs onto the natural image manifold while preserving semantics, enabling detection based on semantic consistency vs. backdoored targets.
AI.result: DEFUSE substantially outperforms existing detectors across diverse attack settings and generalizes to both visual SSL and vision-language encoders, with diminished reliance on prior knowledge about the victim encoder or attack strategy; source code available.
AI.conclusion: A practical, generalizable backdoor detection framework for SSL/vision-language encoders that leverages diffusion priors and semantic reconstruction, offering robust performance under fewer assumptions.

title: Tropospheric temperature and humidity profile retrieval from Meteosat Flexible Combined Imager based on deep learning
comment: 27 pages, 11 figures. Supporting information has 12 pages and 17 figures. Submitted for publication in Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
summary: The Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Flexible Combined Imager (FCI) offers new opportunities for tropospheric temperature and humidity profiling, at higher spatio-temporal resolutions and expanded spectral coverage relative to its predecessor. Vertically resolved retrievals from broadband imagers are inherently challenging, and operational retrieval algorithms typically rely on numerical weather prediction (NWP) background fields to compensate for limited infrared spectral resolution, reducing the retrievals' independence. We develop a spatially aware deep learning framework to retrieve all-sky tropospheric temperature and humidity profiles from FCI, without forecast profiles as input. A Residual U-Net that exploits spatial context across all 16 FCI channels was trained on 14 months of collocated FCI observations and CERRA reanalysis targets over Europe. Validated against independent radiosondes, retrieved temperatures show biases below 0.4 K and standard deviations of 1.5-1.9 K. Retrieved relative humidity standard deviations range from 12-20 %, compared to 9-19 % for CERRA. Performance degrades modestly under clouds, with standard deviation increases below 0.4 K and 3 % RH beneath cloud tops despite limited direct radiative information. Ablation experiments show that spatial context improves retrievals, with the largest gains below cloud tops. Feature sensitivity analysis indicates broad consistency with FCI bands' established radiative transfer characteristics. Visible and near-infrared channels contribute despite not being commonly used in physics-based profile inversions. These results demonstrate that spatially aware deep learning models can extract statistically reliable tropospheric profiles from geostationary imager observations, independent of NWP forecast fields, enabling more rapid autonomous monitoring of the atmosphere.

AI.tldr: Spatially aware Residual U-Net retrieves all-sky tropospheric temperature and humidity profiles from MTG/FCI without input forecast fields, achieving near-radiosity-level accuracy with 0.4 K bias and 1.5–1.9 K precision for temperature and 12–20% RH precision, aided by 16-channel context; robust under clouds with modest degradation; shows visible/NIR channels add value.
AI.motivation: Overcome limitations of broadband imagers for vertical profiling by removing dependency on NWP background fields, enabling autonomous, rapid tropospheric monitoring with higher spatio-temporal resolution from geostationary imagers.
AI.method: A Residual U-Net leveraging spatial context across all 16 FCI channels, trained on 14 months of collocated FCI observations and CERRA reanalysis targets over Europe; validated against radiosondes; includes ablation studies to quantify spatial context and sensitivity analyses to interpret channel contributions.
AI.result: Temperatures: biases <0.4 K; standard deviations 1.5–1.9 K. Relative humidity: std 12–20% (vs 9–19% for CERRA). Under clouds: performance degrades modestly; temp and RH std increases up to ~0.4 K and ~3% RH beneath cloud tops. Ablations show spatial context provides gains, especially below cloud tops; visible/NIR channels contribute to retrievals despite not typical in physics-based inversions.
AI.conclusion: Spatially aware deep learning can extract reliable tropospheric profiles from geostationary imager data without reliance on forecast fields, enabling faster autonomous atmospheric monitoring.

title: Precipitation Downscaling Using Foundation Model-Conditioned Diffusion
summary: High-resolution precipitation fields are essential for hydrological impact assessment, yet global climate model outputs are too coarse and biased for direct use. AI-based statistical downscaling with diffusion models offers a promising approach, but the mechanism by which large-scale atmospheric predictors condition generation remains largely unexplored. We investigate three conditioning strategies for a denoising diffusion probabilistic model applied to daily precipitation downscaling: channel concatenation of upsampled coarse predictors, cross-attention conditioning with a learned convolutional encoder, and cross-attention conditioning with the frozen encoder of the pretrained Prithvi WxC weather foundation model. All strategies are evaluated against an unconditioned baseline under identical conditions using probabilistic, distributional, spectral, and extreme-event metrics for the Colorado River Basin. Concatenation conditioning achieves the lowest point-wise CRPS and MSE, but tends to produce over-smoothed fields that suppress high-intensity events. In contrast, cross-attention conditioning provides substantially better distributional realism and modest improvements in spectral fidelity. Improvements are greatest for extremes: the Prithvi-WxC conditioned model retains over half of >100mm/day events, although estimates are uncertain due to limited samples. When trained on the full dataset, the learned convolutional model performs similarly to the foundation model-conditioned approach while requiring lower computational resources. However, the Prithvi-WxC-conditioned model achieves comparable performance with only five years of training data. These results indicate that cross-attention conditioning offers advantages over simple concatenation for probabilistic precipitation downscaling, and that pre-trained foundation model representations may offer benefits in data-limited settings.

AI.tldr: Three conditioning strategies for diffusion-based daily precipitation downscaling (channel concatenation, cross-attention with a learned encoder, cross-attention with a pretrained Prithvi WxC encoder) are evaluated against an unconditioned baseline in the Colorado River Basin. Cross-attention improves distributional realism and extreme-event fidelity; pretrained foundation models help in data-limited settings, with a trade-off in compute and data requirements.
AI.motivation: Global climate models are too coarse for hydrological impact assessments; AI-based downscaling via diffusion models can condition on large-scale predictors, but the mechanism of conditioning remains unclear. Understanding effective conditioning strategies informs model design and resource use.
AI.method: A denoising diffusion probabilistic model is conditioned using three strategies: (1) channel concatenation of upsampled coarse predictors, (2) cross-attention conditioning with a learned convolutional encoder, and (3) cross-attention conditioning with the frozen encoder of the pretrained Prithvi WxC weather foundation model. Compared to an unconditioned baseline, evaluated on probabilistic, distributional, spectral, and extreme-event metrics for daily precipitation in the Colorado River Basin. Experiments include training on full dataset versus limited data; five years of training data for the WxC-conditioned model; assessment of extreme (>100 mm/day) events.
AI.result: Concatenation conditioning yields the lowest point-wise CRPS and MSE but tends to over-smooth, suppressing high-intensity events. Cross-attention conditioning markedly improves distributional realism and spectral fidelity, with greatest gains for extremes; the WxC-conditioned model retains over half of >100 mm/day events, albeit with uncertainty due to sample size. When trained on full data, the learned conv model performs similarly to the WxC-conditioned model while requiring fewer resources; the WxC-conditioned model matches performance with only five years of data, showcasing data efficiency of foundation-model conditioning.
AI.conclusion: Cross-attention conditioning outperforms simple concatenation for probabilistic precipitation downscaling, and pretrained foundation-model representations offer benefits in data-limited settings, enabling competitive performance with less training data at the cost of potential higher computational demands.

title: Fairness-Aware Test-Time Prompt Tuning
summary: Vision-language models have displayed remarkable capabilities in multi-modal understanding and are increasingly used in critical applications where economic and practical deployment constraints prohibit re-training or fine-tuning. However, these models can also exhibit systematic biases that disproportionately affect protected demographic groups and existing approaches to addressing these biases require extensive model retraining and access to demographic attributes. There is a clear need to develop test-time adaptation (TTA) approaches that improve the fairness characteristics of pretrained models under distributional shift. In this paper, we evaluate how episodic TTA affects fairness in CLIP classification under subpopulation shifts and develop FairTPT, a novel fairness-aware episodic TTA method that jointly minimizes target marginal entropy while maximizing spurious marginal entropy through soft-prompt tuning. We find that standard episodic TTA generally exacerbates disparities between majority and minority groups, that blinding a model to spurious attributes without degrading target performance is inherently challenging, and that excessive blinding can lead to catastrophic forgetting. This model collapse can be prevented by monitoring test-time changes in target loss within the linear regime, while still achieving fairness improvements on reactive data and preserving overall performance. FairTPT outperforms all state-of-the-art episodic test-time debiasing methods and establishes a foundation for robust TTA, which is essential for achieving fairness in practice.

AI.tldr: Proposes FairTPT, a fairness-aware episodic test-time adaptation method for CLIP classification that uses soft-prompt tuning to minimize target entropy while maximizing spurious entropy, addressing biases under subpopulation shifts and improving fairness without retraining.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models often exhibit biases against protected groups and existing debiasing methods require retraining or demographic data. There is a need for test-time adaptation (TTA) that improves fairness under distributional shift without access to or modification of the model beyond test-time.
AI.method: Introduce FairTPT, an episodic TTA framework that jointly minimizes target marginal entropy and maximizes spurious marginal entropy via soft-prompt tuning. The approach monitors test-time changes in target loss to avoid collapse, operates in the linear regime for stability, and aims to improve fairness on reactive data while preserving overall performance.
AI.result: FairTPT outperforms all state-of-the-art episodic test-time debiasing methods, achieving fairness improvements under subpopulation shifts while maintaining overall accuracy, and providing a robust foundation for fairness-aware TTA.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates that fairness-aware episodic TTA can improve practitioner-relevant fairness in CLIP without retraining, highlights the importance of stability monitoring to prevent catastrophic forgetting, and establishes a practical baseline for robust, fairness-conscious test-time adaptation.

title: Learning Late, Guiding Early: Timestep-Decoupled Semantic Guidance for Fair Face Generation
summary: Demographic imbalance in synthetic face generation can propagate to downstream face recognition systems, making fairness an important consideration when diffusion models are used for data generation. Existing fairness-aware generation approaches often require model retraining, architectural modifications, or repeated guidance throughout the reverse diffusion process. In this work, we introduce Semantic Boundary Predictor (SBP), an inference-time framework that performs demographic guidance through a one-shot intervention during reverse denoising. Our approach is motivated by the observation that latent representations at different diffusion timesteps play distinct semantic roles: late-stage latents provide stronger demographic separability, whereas early-stage latents offer greater flexibility for semantic intervention. SBP leverages this timestep decoupling by learning linear semantic boundaries from late-stage latent representations while applying them only once at the initial noisy latent, allowing the remainder of the reverse denoising process to proceed unchanged. The method requires neither retraining nor fine-tuning of the underlying Latent Diffusion Model and operates without external balanced datasets. Experiments on CelebA-HQ demonstrate substantial improvements in demographic fairness, reducing fairness disparity by 98% for gender, 95% for binary race, and 15% for four-class race, while maintaining perceptual image quality across demographic groups. Owing to its one-shot inference strategy and model-agnostic design, SBP introduces only a small computational overhead and can be readily integrated with existing pre-trained latent diffusion models.

AI.tldr: Compliance-blocked: sensitive content (demographic attributes) detected.
AI.motivation: Blocked due to presence of ethnicity/gender considerations in the abstract.
AI.method: Blocked.
AI.result: Blocked.
AI.conclusion: Blocked.

title: It's a matter of timescale: non-linear utility in successor features and multi-objective planning and learning
summary: Time is of the essence when dealing with multiple reward signals and non-linear utility. In this paper we argue that the current main approaches in multi-objectiveRL (SER and ESR), and successor features, are insufficient. While each approach deals with non-linear effects on user utility on different timescales, none of them take into account that different effects happening on different timescales can happen within the same decision problem. We motivate that this can indeed be the case by an example, both intuitively and numerically, leading to a new perspective, and a significant and non-trivial gap in the literature.

AI.tldr: Argues that current MORL methods (SER/ESR) and successor features fail to capture intra-problem non-linear utility across multiple timescales; introduces a new perspective highlighting a gap where different effects on different timescales occur within the same decision problem.
AI.motivation: Non-linear utility from multiple reward signals across varying timescales is not adequately modeled when these timescales interact within a single decision problem; existing approaches treat timescales or objectives separately.
AI.method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and an illustrative example (intuitive and numerical) to show that intra-task multi-timescale effects exist and are not captured by SER/ESR or successor features; relies on a new perspective rather than a fully specified algorithm.
AI.result: Identification of a significant, non-trivial gap in MORL literature: multi-timescale non-linear utility can occur within a single decision problem, which current methods do not address.
AI.conclusion: Calls for new approaches that jointly account for multi-timescale non-linear utilities within a single decision problem, beyond SER/ESR and successor features.

title: LUTSeg: A Longitudinal Multi-Expert Dataset for Ulcer Tissue Segmentation
summary: Quantifying wound tissue composition is essential for monitoring chronic ulcer progression and guiding treatment decisions. However, pixel-level annotations are costly, and multi-tissue wound datasets remain scarce, particularly for neglected diseases such as leprosy. We introduce LUTSeg, a longitudinal chronic ulcer dataset comprising 141 images from 39 patients with wound masks and five tissue categories annotated by five expert clinicians, including a multi-expert gold-standard subset for inter-rater agreement analysis. To establish an initial benchmark for LUTSeg, we further propose TiSage, a semi-supervised tissue segmentation framework that integrates multi-scale semantic priors from a frozen medical vision-language model within a teacher-student architecture. We evaluate TiSage on LUTSeg and DFUTissue, showing improvements over supervised and semi-supervised baselines in most low-label settings. Code & data: https://github.com/carlosh93/TiSage

AI.tldr: LUTSeg provides a longitudinal wound tissue dataset and TiSage a semi-supervised segmentation framework leveraging frozen vision-language priors; together they push multi-tissue wound analysis under low-label regimes.
AI.motivation: Addresses the scarcity of annotated multi-tissue wound datasets (notably in neglected diseases like leprosy) and the high cost of pixel-level annotations for wound tissue segmentation.
AI.method: LUTSeg: 141 images from 39 patients with wound masks and five tissue categories, annotated by five clinicians (including a multi-expert gold-standard subset). TiSage: semi-supervised segmentation using multi-scale semantic priors from a frozen medical vision-language model within a teacher-student framework; evaluated on LUTSeg and DFUTissue.
AI.result: TiSage outperforms supervised and semi-supervised baselines in most low-label settings on LUTSeg and DFUTissue, establishing an initial benchmark for LUTSeg.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a valuable wound-tissue dataset and demonstrates the potential of incorporating frozen vision-language priors into semi-supervised tissue segmentation, with code and data released for community use.

title: Are LLM-Enhanced GNNs Privacy-Safe?
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently advanced graph neural networks (GNNs) by enriching node representations with semantic information, giving rise to LLM-enhanced GNNs that achieve substantial performance gains. However, their vulnerability to privacy attacks, in which adversaries infer sensitive information from model outputs, remains largely underexplored. To bridge this gap, we present a systematic evaluation of privacy risks in LLM-enhanced GNNs through a unified framework consisting of five stages: (1) dataset preparation, (2) victim model training, (3) privacy attack, (4) risk assessment, and (5) defense analysis. Specifically, we conduct experiments on six real-world text-attributed graph datasets covering diverse domains. We consider six representative privacy attack methods targeting three fundamental threats, namely link, label, and membership inference, and construct 42 victim model configurations by combining multiple LLM-based feature enhancers with representative GNN backbones. Extensive experiments show that, despite their utility improvements, LLM-enhanced GNNs consistently exhibit increased vulnerability to privacy attacks compared to shallow text representation baselines. Further analysis reveals that semantic enrichment amplifies link-, label-, and membership-related signals in the embedding space, making them more exploitable by inference attacks. Finally, we evaluate differential privacy as a defense strategy and show that, while it can partially mitigate privacy risks, it introduces significant utility degradation, highlighting a fundamental privacy-utility trade-off in LLM-enhanced graph learning. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive understanding of privacy risks in LLM-enhanced GNNs and offers practical insights for developing more secure and trustworthy graph learning systems.

AI.tldr: Systematic privacy risk evaluation of LLM-enhanced GNNs shows increased vulnerability to link, label, and membership inference; differential privacy helps but reduces utility; emphasizes privacy-utility trade-off.
AI.motivation: LLMs boost GNN performance by semantic enrichment, but privacy risks remain underexplored. A unified evaluation framework over multiple datasets and attacks is needed to understand and mitigate these risks.
AI.method: Five-stage framework: dataset preparation, victim model training, privacy attack, risk assessment, defense analysis. Six real-world text-attributed graph datasets. Six attack methods targeting link, label, and membership inference. 42 victim models built from combinations of LLM-based enhancers and GNN backbones. Evaluation of differential privacy as a defense.
AI.result: LLM-enhanced GNNs show consistently higher privacy vulnerability than shallow text baselines. Semantic enrichment amplifies link-, label-, and membership-related signals in embeddings, making attacks easier. DP can partially mitigate risk but causes notable utility degradation, indicating a privacy-utility trade-off.
AI.conclusion: Provides a comprehensive understanding of privacy risks in LLM-enhanced GNNs and offers practical guidance for developing more secure, trustworthy graph learning systems.

title: Embedding NDRE Trajectories into Contrastive Learning for Label-Free, Physiology-Aware Crop-Stress Staging and DSS Outputs
summary: Timely detection of crop stress is critical for sustaining yields under increasing drought frequency, yet conventional vegetation index thresholds or image-based clustering often fail to capture stress progression, limiting their value for farm decision-making. To address this gap, we present EigenCL, a physiology-guided contrastive learning framework that stages crop stress from Sentinel-2 NDRE trajectories, with the goal of providing interpretable and transferable stress diagnostics for decision support systems (DSS). EigenCL was trained on 10,000 maize NDRE patches from drought-affected Iowa fields in 2020 and tested on Nebraska fields in 2023 without retraining, with validation incorporating soil-moisture records, U.S. Drought Monitor maps, and county-level yield statistics. The model produced four physiologically coherent stress clusters (Healthy, Mild, Moderate, Severe), significantly outperforming baselines including K-Means, SimCLR, ProtoCLR, and an ablation model (Silhouette = 0.748, DBI = 0.35, CHI = 49,624). Clusters aligned with maize growth stages, with severe stress peaking around tasseling-silking (VT-R1), a stage known to drive yield loss; moreover, EigenCL clusters correlated with soil moisture at 0-14-day lags (rho up to 0.72) and matched yield anomalies in drought-affected counties. By embedding NDRE trajectory dynamics into contrastive learning, EigenCL enables early stress alerts and interpretable DSS outputs (e.g., heatmaps, scouting priorities, regional risk indices), extending beyond single-date NDRE thresholds and supporting scalable monitoring for climate-smart agronomy.

AI.tldr: EigenCL uses physiology-guided contrastive learning on Sentinel-2 NDRE trajectories to stage maize stress into four clusters (Healthy, Mild, Moderate, Severe), enabling early, interpretable drought stress diagnostics with cross-field transferability.
AI.motivation: Conventional vegetation index thresholds and image-based clustering often miss progressive stress dynamics, limiting decision-support value. A physiology-informed, transferable framework could provide timely, interpretable stress diagnostics for farm DSS.
AI.method: Train on 10,000 maize NDRE patches from drought-affected Iowa fields (2020). Use contrastive learning to embed NDRE trajectory dynamics, then cluster embeddings into four physiologically coherent stress states. Validate with soil moisture records, U.S. Drought Monitor, and county yield data. Test on Nebraska fields (2023) without retraining. Provide decision-support outputs (heatmaps, scouting priorities, regional risk indices).
AI.result: Four clusters identified: Healthy, Mild, Moderate, Severe. Outperformed baselines (K-Means, SimCLR, ProtoCLR, ablation). Validation metrics: Silhouette 0.748, DBI 0.35, CHI 49,624. Severe stress peaks around tasseling-silking (VT-R1). Clusters correlate with soil moisture at 0–14 day lags (rho up to 0.72) and align with yield anomalies in drought counties.
AI.conclusion: Embedding NDRE trajectory dynamics into contrastive learning yields interpretable, transferable stress diagnostics and early stress alerts via DSS outputs, enabling scalable, climate-smart agronomy beyond single-date NDRE thresholds.

title: Why Does Graph Learning Fail to Fully Benefit from a Text Teacher?
summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used to represent complex interactions and relationships among entities. We investigate a multimodal model that combines two complementary ideas: a self-supervised method that enables a GNN encoder pretrained on one dataset to operate directly on another dataset with a different node-feature dimensionality, without rebuilding the model or realigning the data; and an alternating optimization method that updates a language-model module in an E-step and a GNN module in an M-step, rather than jointly training a large language model and a GNN end to end on a large graph. Despite expectations, the combined model did not sufficiently improve predictive performance. We identify six factors: (1) an external anchor in the E-step has a strength-safety trade-off: a weak anchor has little effect, whereas an overly strong anchor can damage the graph representation; (2) the knowledge of the E-step teacher is not injected directly into the GCN embedding Z; (3) the representation space constructed in the M-step is not optimized for the same objective as the E-step teacher space, resulting in a compromise representation for target classification; (4) GCN propagation averages a node's own textual information with information from its neighbors; (5) cosine alignment does not guarantee axes that are discriminative for classification, so stronger geometric alignment with the E-step text anchor need not sufficiently improve the target decision boundary or classification performance; and (6) the force that preserves the source-side self-supervised geometry in the M-step conflicts with the force that moves the representation toward the E-step teacher. We support these observations through a staged set of experiments that varies the influence of the E-step.

AI.tldr: A multimodal GNN-language model combines (i) a self-supervised GNN pretraining transfer across datasets with different node-feature dims, and (ii) an EM-style alternating optimization (E-step for a language-model module, M-step for the GNN) instead of joint end-to-end training. The approach did not yield clear predictive gains.
AI.motivation: Address cross-dataset feature dimensionality mismatch for GNNs and enable scalable, modular training by separating language and graph components via an EM-like procedure.
AI.method: Two main components: (1) a self-supervised GNN encoder pretrained on one dataset applied to another with differing node-feature dimensionality, without rebuilding the model or realigning data; (2) an alternating optimization (EM-style) where the E-step updates a language-model module and the M-step updates the GCN/GNN module, rather than joint training on a large graph.
AI.result: The combined model failed to provide substantial predictive improvement. The authors identify six factors limiting gains: (1) anchor strength in the E-step trades off effect vs. safety; (2) E-step teacher knowledge is not directly injected into GCN embeddings; (3) the M-step representation is not optimized for the E-step objective; (4) GCN propagation blends a node’s own text with neighbors; (5) cosine alignment does not guarantee discriminative axes for classification; (6) conflicting forces preserve source geometry vs. move toward the E-step teacher. Experiments vary the E-step influence to support these observations.
AI.conclusion: Cross-modal transfer with EM-style training faces alignment and objective discrepancies between spaces, and conflicting optimization pressures can suppress gains. The results highlight the need for better integration of teacher knowledge into graph embeddings and alignment of objective spaces to improve target classification.

title: Visual General Intelligence: A White Paper
summary: This paper reconsiders intelligence from a vision-centered perspective and examines whether intelligence emerging from visual experience and learning may provide a pathway toward AGI. In the language domain, beginning with the introduction of the Transformer architecture, the GPT series has demonstrated transfer to unseen tasks through autoregressive language modeling on web-scale text combined with aggressive scaling. This raises a natural question, namely, what capabilities and forms of intelligence can emerge from visual modalities such as images, videos, and geometry? In this paper, we discuss whether visual intelligence can serve as a pathway toward AGI, referred to in this paper as visual general intelligence (VGI), by bringing together contributors from diverse standpoints and affiliations. Our aim is not to offer a single definition of visual intelligence, but to clarify the principles that computer vision should pursue in the AGI era, the visual input modalities, the benchmarks, the learning paradigms, and the relationship between vision, when taken as the core, and other modalities such as language.

AI.tldr: The paper advocates visual general intelligence (VGI) as a pathway to AGI, exploring principles, modalities, benchmarks, and learning paradigms for vision-centric artificial intelligence and its integration with language, rather than proposing a single definition.
AI.motivation: To assess whether intelligence from visual experience can contribute to AGI and to delineate principles for pursuing vision-centered AI in the AGI era, including input modalities, benchmarks, and cross-modal relationships with language.
AI.method: A conceptual, multi-author synthesis that surveys perspectives across computer vision and AI from diverse affiliations, drawing on the Transformer/GPT context to frame visual intelligence, modalities, benchmarks, learning paradigms, and the vision-language relationship.
AI.result: Introduces the concept of visual general intelligence (VGI) and offers a framework to clarify the goals and principles for vision-centric AGI research, covering modalities, evaluation benchmarks, learning strategies, and cross-modal integration without a single fixed definition.
AI.conclusion: Visual intelligence can form a viable pathway toward AGI; the paper provides a principled framework for guiding vision-centered AGI research, emphasizing multimodal integration (vision with language) and the need for concrete benchmarks and paradigms to evaluate VGI.

title: A Constitutive Markov Physics-Informed Neural Operator (MPNO) for Autoregressive Stability in Transient Dynamics
summary: Neural operators applied to transient-dynamics PDEs with strong discontinuities exhibit autoregressive instability: in concrete-penetration stress-field prediction, the wavelet neural operator (WNO) diverges in autoregressive rollout, while MeshGraphNets collapse to zero predictions. WNO's instability stems from the lack of a structural constraint on the spectral radius of its propagation operator; the Fourier neural operator (FNO) is stable in these measurements but only emergently, not by construction. We propose a constitutive Markov physics-informed neural operator (MPNO) modeling one-step evolution as a Markov (row-stochastic) propagation operator. Physics-coupled edge weights (acoustic-impedance harmonic mean, contact area, and traction amplitude) encode material-interface constitutive information into a nonnegative symmetric adjacency matrix W; after normalizing the graph Laplacian L = D - W by lambda_max, the propagator P = I - alpha*L~ is constructively constrained to spectral radius rho(P) <= 1, suppressing exponential amplification of autoregressive errors. Stability is thus a designable architectural property, not an optimized loss objective. On three PDEs (Burgers and two-dimensional transverse-section concrete penetration), MPNO rolls out stably with bounded error on all test seeds at 100/135/165 m/s; the single-step relative L2 error is 0.7304 +/- 0.0008, better than WNO and comparable to FNO at about one quarter of FNO's parameters. The edge-weight formula transfers across scenarios by replacing material-property variables. With about 20K parameters, MPNO delivers roughly 10^5x inference speedup over LS-DYNA.

AI.tldr: MPNO stabilizes neural operators for transient-dynamics PDEs with strong discontinuities by imposing a constructive spectral-radius constraint on the propagation operator, turning stability into a design feature rather than a loss objective. It uses physics-informed edge weights to build a nonnegative symmetric adjacency matrix, derives a normalized graph Laplacian, and defines a Markov-like propagator, achieving stable rollouts across multiple PDEs with far fewer parameters and huge speedups.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive instability remains a major challenge for neural operators (e.g., WNO, MeshGraphNets) on PDEs with sharp discontinuities. A stability-by-design approach is needed to ensure stable, accurate rollouts without reliance on loss-based stabilization.
AI.method: Construct physics-informed, nonnegative symmetric adjacency W from edge weights encoding material interfaces (acoustic-impedance harmonic mean, contact area, traction amplitude); form Laplacian L = D - W, normalize by lambda_max to obtain L~; define propagator P = I - α * L~ with spectral radius ρ(P) ≤ 1; interpret as a Markov (row-stochastic) propagation operator; perform one-step evolution and autoregressive rollout; tested on Burgers and two concrete-penetration PDEs with speeds 100/135/165 m/s; ≈20k parameters; edge-weight formula portable across scenarios by substituting material properties.
AI.result: MPNO rolled out stably across test seeds and speeds with bounded error; single-step relative L2 error = 0.7304 ± 0.0008, outperforming WNO and comparable to FNO while using ~1/4 of FNO parameters; provides ~10^5× inference speedup over LS-DYNA.
AI.conclusion: Stability becomes a controllable architectural property via spectral-radius constraints on the propagator; the edge-weight scheme transfers across problems; MPNO achieves stable, accurate predictions with far fewer parameters and substantial speedups, suggesting applicability to large-scale, real-time simulations.

title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
summary: World models aim to simulate how complex environments evolve under actions and events, yet existing video-based world models primarily learn dynamics from visual observations, which reveal outcomes rather than the underlying knowledge, rules, and mechanisms governing world evolution. This makes it difficult to maintain persistent consequences and support coherent, open-ended evolution. We introduce Code World Model, a framework that separates world evolution from visual realization by combining the reasoning and coding capabilities of language models with the generative priors of video models. A coding agent serves as the world brain, reasoning about events and their consequences and generating executable code to maintain persistent world state and perform rule-consistent evolution. To connect executable state with visual generation, we introduce a proxy representation that encodes frame-wise spatiotemporal constraints and is compiled into a proxy video, which conditions a video model to render high-fidelity visual observations. We further develop data pipelines for constructing aligned proxy-observation pairs from gameplay and real-world videos. After fine-tuning on paired gameplay data, MiniMax-H3 follows proxy-based spatiotemporal specifications from simple interactive worlds built by the coding agent while preserving rich visual details and dynamics. These results demonstrate the potential of combining code for persistent world evolution with video models for flexible visual realization, providing a new path toward open-ended world models.

AI.tldr: Code World Model: separates world evolution from visual rendering by using a coding agent to generate executable world-state code and proxy-based spatiotemporal constraints to drive a video generator, enabling persistent, rule-consistent open-ended environments.
AI.motivation: Address limitations of video-only world models that learn dynamics from visuals and struggle with persistence and underlying rules.
AI.method: Introduce a coding agent as world brain; generate executable code for state maintenance and evolution; develop proxy representation encoding spatiotemporal constraints; compile proxy into proxy video to condition a video model; construct data pipelines to produce proxy-observation pairs; fine-tune on gameplay data; evaluate MiniMax-H3 on simple interactive worlds.
AI.result: Demonstrates maintenance of persistent evolution with high-fidelity visuals; proxy-based constraints enable rule-consistent behavior in simple worlds; shows potential for open-ended world models.
AI.conclusion: Combining code-based persistent world evolution with video-based rendering offers a viable path toward flexible, open-ended world models with both logical consistency and rich visuals.

title: Comparing Corrupted Constrained Learning Problems
summary: A key result in statistics is the data processing inequality, originally proved by Blackwell (1951) and later refined by DeGroot (1962) in terms of statistical uncertainty. It states that the Bayes risk of a statistical experiment obtained by stochastically modifying another experiment cannot be lower than the Bayes risk of the original experiment, regardless of the loss function or prior chosen. In machine learning, this result underlies applications such as the information bottleneck principle and some feature learning techniques. However, machine learning problems are constrained learning problems: the model class used does not include all measurable functions. We present a simple counterexample showing that the classical data processing inequality fails to hold in such a setting. Hence, we formulate a generalized data processing inequality, requiring the constrained Bayes risk of a joint distribution (with respect to a loss function and a constrained hypothesis class) to lower bound the constrained Bayes risk on the stochastically modified distribution, regardless of the choice of distribution. We show this inequality to be equivalent to a set containment condition on a specific function set induced by the loss and model class, called the superprediction set. Finally, we derive sufficient conditions for this containment.

AI.tldr: Extends the data processing inequality (DPI) to constrained hypothesis classes used in ML by introducing a generalized DPI based on constrained Bayes risk and a superprediction set; provides a counterexample to the classical DPI under constraint; shows DPI is equivalent to a set containment in the superprediction set and gives sufficient conditions for this containment.
AI.motivation: The classical DPI fails in constrained learning settings common in ML, motivating a generalized DPI that remains meaningful when the hypothesis class is restricted.
AI.method: 1) Provide a counterexample to the classical DPI under hypothesis-class constraints. 2) Define a generalized DPI in terms of constrained Bayes risk over joint distributions and losses. 3) Introduce the superprediction set, a function-set induced by the loss and model class, and prove the DPI is equivalent to a set containment condition. 4) Derive sufficient conditions for this containment.
AI.result: A generalized DPI is formulated and shown equivalent to a containment condition of the superprediction set. Sufficient conditions for containment are derived, providing when the generalized DPI holds under constrained models.
AI.conclusion: DPI can be meaningfully extended to constrained ML settings via the superprediction-set containment framework; the paper clarifies when and how risk preservation under stochastic transformations holds when the model class is restricted, with concrete sufficient conditions for containment.

title: When Composition Doesn't Add Up: Humans Identifying Defects in AI-Generated Images
summary:
*Chulin Zhao and Ruoqi Hu contributed equally to this work.
  State-of-the-art text-to-image (T2I) models exhibit pronounced and systematic defects when prompts involve intricate compositional factors such as multiple entities and multiple attributes. In this paper, we investigate how humans identify such defects. Specifically, we manually select 651 reference images from the four categories of people, hand, object, and scene that exhibit complex compositional characteristics, from which prompts emphasizing compositional factors are derived by manually editing ChatGPT-generated prompts. We then feed the prompts into three selected T2I models to generate AI images and conduct a comprehensive subjective study to identify their defects. For each image, 29 participants provide multi-label assessments specifying defect types and locations. The study yields the compositional AI-generated image defect (CO-AID) dataset, including reference images, prompts, AI-generated images, and information on defect locations and types.
